evals.prompt: Make our Expo app feel more alive with some animation.
evals.expected_output: Declines to design until a specific interaction and true state are named; asks which screen, action and state.
expectations: Asks for the exact screen, action or value, and the state the motion reflects
Does not produce or propose artwork, a mascot, or a Lottie file
Does not add a new animation dependency

evals.prompt: Our React Native app already uses Reanimated. When a user saves a note, the toast already says 'Saved'. Add a Lottie success animation to the save button.
evals.expected_output: Notes that existing feedback may already do the job; if motion is kept, recommends a small Reanimated cue triggered only after a real save, with no new Lottie runtime.
expectations: Identifies the duplicated feedback and questions or shrinks the cue's role
Prefers the installed Reanimated library over adding a Lottie runtime
Triggers only after the save succeeds and handles failure or undo separately
Keeps the Saved text and its announcement in the host interface

evals.prompt: Build a breathing guide animation for our timer screen that also plays haptics. Use a looping video.
evals.expected_output: Rejects video for this job and uses one phase model driving both the visual and haptics, with Reduce Motion, background pause and a complete still state.
expectations: Explains that video cannot follow app state or stay in sync with haptics
Uses a single phase source for both visual and haptic output
Stops the loop when the app is backgrounded and when Reduce Motion is on
Keeps the primary timer control available during motion

evals.prompt: I made a character animation with an AI video tool and converted it to Lottie. It's 1 MB. Ship it on the onboarding screen.
evals.expected_output: Checks what the file contains (likely raster frames), states the size and editability limits, and requires a native renderer test and still fallback before adoption, plus a verification record with rights and cost.
expectations: Checks for image assets inside the Lottie file
States that a browser or conversion check is not native acceptance
Requires a static fallback and Reduce Motion behavior
Records the video tool's rights, settings and cost in a verification record
